description: Sole AI egress point for the suite: task-class policy, data protection, and cost accounting.
_doc: In-tree manifest for KisaesDevLab/Vibe-AI-Router (github.com/KisaesDevLab/Vibe-AI-Router), current release v0.0.2 (0.0.2 role-gates /metrics and all background jobs to the gateway, so the deny_paths and CATALOG_SYNC_CRON entries below are defense in depth for older images, not the only line). Replaces the scrapped Vibe-Shield concept with routing-layer enforcement; inherits Shield's :5193 emergency port (returned to the pool 2026-07-24). TWO containers from one image (ROUTER_ROLE): the CONSOLE (8222) is the staff admin UI and is the only surface Caddy fronts; the GATEWAY (8220) serves /v1 for other Vibe apps and is never routed publicly — apps reach it by container DNS on vibe_net. Splitting the roles is what allows the console to have TLS without publishing the gateway with it. NOT YET WIRED: no other app's env template points at the gateway (they still carry their own ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), so the router is installed and usable from its own console but is not yet the suite's actual egress path — that needs per-app support for the app-token + X-Vibe-Task-Class contract in each app's image. See docs/PHASES.md.

subdomains.name: airouter
subdomains.emergencyNote: The ONLY way in on LAN/Tailscale (rootServedOnly: no path mount). In domain mode cookies are Secure, so plain-HTTP sign-in fails here — use it to confirm the service is up, then fix TLS/DNS.

health_extra.name: gateway
health_extra.doc: The /v1 surface other apps call. It has no Caddy vhost, so without this entry nothing would ever probe it — the console can be healthy while the gateway is down.

required.name: MASTER_KEY
required.doc: Vault master key. Wraps every per-credential data key; losing it means re-entering every provider API key. Generated once and preserved across re-renders. EXCLUDED from the Vault backup set by design — escrow separately (the app's docs/runbook.md).

required.name: SESSION_SECRET
required.doc: Signs admin console session cookies. Rendered from the appliance-wide JWT_SECRET in shared.env (the same convention vibe-connect / vibe-tx-converter use for their SESSION_SECRET), not a per-app value. Rotating shared.env's JWT_SECRET just signs everyone out here.

required.name: ROUTER_ADMIN_PASSWORD
required.doc: First-login password for the admin console, generated on enable and surfaced in the console's first-login card and in /opt/vibe/CREDENTIALS.txt (the per-app first-login section, written from firstLogin.passwordEnvKey).

optional.name: ROUTER_ADMIN_EMAIL
optional.doc: Login for the router's admin console. Set this BEFORE first enable if you want a real address — the bootstrap that creates the admin runs exactly once (state.apps.<slug>.seeded gates it), so changing this later creates nothing and the original login stays. To adopt a new address afterwards, add the admin from inside the router's console.

ui.label: Router admin email
ui.helpText: The email you sign in with at the AI Router console. Set it before you enable the app — after that the first-run bootstrap has already created the admin and won't run again.

optional.name: LOCAL_MODEL_BASE_URL
optional.doc: OpenAI-compatible endpoint of the appliance's own model server. Must stay a LAN/docker address — the router rejects a 'local' provider pointed at a public host (that would be a covert cloud route around the data boundary).

ui.label: Local model server URL
ui.helpText: Where the on-appliance model server listens, e.g. http://vibellm:11434/v1. Every local-only task class is served from here and never leaves the appliance.

optional.name: LOCAL_MODEL_ID
optional.doc: Canonical id (family/native-name) of the model the local server actually serves. Registered as a custom catalog entry at $0 and used as the default for every local-only task class.

ui.label: Local model
ui.helpText: The model your local server serves, as family/name (e.g. ollama/qwen3:14b). This is what classification, extraction, and other local-only tasks run on.

optional.name: SCRUBBER_MODE_NOTE
optional.doc: Placeholder: the scrubber mode is firm state, edited in the router's own console (Firm settings), not an env var. Listed here so operators searching Settings for it are pointed at the right place.

firstLogin.note: In domain mode, sign in at https://airouter.<your-domain>/ — this app is served at the ROOT of its own subdomain in BOTH routing modes (its bundle can't be path-mounted; see rootServedOnly). In LAN/Tailscale mode there is no such hostname: use http://<server-ip>:5193/ from the LAN or tailnet. The username is whatever ROUTER_ADMIN_EMAIL was at enable time. Change the password inside the router's console after first sign-in — the appliance's first-run bootstrap runs once and will not reset it again (not even on disable/re-enable). NOTE: only the ADMIN CONSOLE is published — the /v1 gateway other apps call runs in a separate container that is never routed publicly.

seed.description: Production first-run bootstrap: creates the firm, the admin login (ROUTER_ADMIN_PASSWORD), registers the appliance's local model server, populates the model catalog from the image's vendored pricing snapshot, and applies the local-first default policy pack. The script itself is idempotent (a re-run only re-applies the admin password), but the appliance runs it EXACTLY ONCE — state.apps.<slug>.seeded gates it and disable-app never clears that flag. To re-run by hand: sudo docker exec vibe-ai-router-console node dist/src/ops/bootstrap-firm.js. This is NOT the app's dev seed (which creates a demo firm with a published password).
